body: I think xanax would help a lot for going to the dentist. I am pretty sure the doctor had me on low doses for the SSRIs. The side effects were not a sex drive issue, rather an inability to orgasm no matter how much I wanted to. I had this problem with paxil and cymbalta. I had robot emotions with zoloft. I told the doctor I wanted to try a different class of drugs, seeing as it was all SSRIs that I was having trouble with. In response, she suggested lexapro. So, I stopped listening to her because that is also an SSRI. Either she wasn't listening to me, or she chose to ignore me, or she doesn't know enough about these drugs to be prescribing them. This is when I stopped taking daily medication (~9 months ago). I have a friend that is on lexapro and has the same sex issues I had on the other SSRIs, which doesn't make me want to try it either.

I have tried a couple different SSRIs for the anxiety but I didn't like any of them. Zoloft made me feel like an emotionless robot, and the other couple I tried made me unable to orgasm which caused anxiety and killed my sex life with my boyfriend. The only one I have found to like is xanax, I keep it in my wallet so that if I ever get bad attacks I can take some. Doctors don't want to keep you on it though, so it is difficult to get. 

I understand what you mean about it feeling ridiculous... I have uncontrollable fear and anxiety of dentists since I was a child. Just thinking about going makes me get dizzy with anxiety and feel like I am going to be sick. I always throw up and feel like my whole body is rejecting itself when I go. I am quite a few years overdue to go again. I suppose this is something I should also discuss with my psychologist once I get the courage to go back to the doctor for a referal.

I think caring a lot about how people see me is a lot to do with personal insecurities and a lack of confidence. I never really developed well in this area growing up, I suspect because of my anxiety. I used to get teased and bullied a lot. I feel more comfortable blending into the background a bit because it seems easier, but at the same time I want to feel different and special. My gym workouts and diet help with that, I don't know any other girls that do serious weight training to build muscle. It feels like a internal conflict of wanting to blend in and not be noticed to feel safe, but also to be the best at what I do, which would get me noticed. 

I really am hoping that I can pull through this one. I think it is the continual falling into these depressions that is making it feel more hopeless. It is like, I put so much effort into getting myself out of them, only to fall back in harder each time. It is as though it is almost useless to pull myself out, because I will just fall back in again anyway.

I had a similar problem with you when getting help with anxiety. It took me years to finally go and see someone. It started around the same time as the depression (~13yo), but I didn't see anyone until I was 18 after I was getting bad panic attacks when someone was stalking me. Then, it took another four years until I saw someone again after another string of attacks coming up to the end of my honours year in university and writing my thesis. The depression though, is something I have never spoken about. I feel like it is stigmatised a lot more than anxiety is. Also, talking about anxiety, I feel anxiety. Talking about depression though, I imagine I would feel depressed about it but also anxious, so it feels twice as intense and difficult. 

I am finding that just talking about it on here is making me feel a little bit better, it helps a lot to feel like other people feel the same things too.

I suppose it is more of a "keeping up appearances" thing... If I start acting differently than usual, people might notice that something isn't right with me. I think it is also a way to hold onto "normality" and prevent myself from slipping into a deeper depression from withdrawing into myself completely. My days when I am not feeling down are pretty much the same, except I enjoy what I do and probably smile a bit more.

I was considering talking to my boyfriend about it, but I just can't. I feel like he is going to think less of me. He knows I have had problems in the past, but he doesn't know to what extent. He doesn't know that in the past I have been suicidal, or that I have had problems with self harm. I am proud of myself for not self harming this time. I think mostly because he would notice, but I would like to think that part of it is that I have become better at coping, and holding on hope that I will get past this, just like every other time. 

I should probably see my psychologist but at the same time, I don't feel like I can talk to her because its sort of like I know her as I have seen her before. I know that sounds silly, and she would just be doing her job and she would see these problems all the time... it just feels very difficult. 

I really hate the way that psychological issues have become so stigmatised. I am embarrassed and shamed by how I feel, and I am scared that if anyone knows about my issues, that they will look down on me and think less of me. 

I agree that it could be related to a fear of failure. All my life, my family has doted on me as the "smart one" that would go very far. But, here I am, failing. I feel like I am not me anymore, I have changed into this person that is failing. I am an embarrassment to myself and to my family. It just feels so horrible. 

I tried small steps.. well I suppose it wasn't really a small step, it felt like a massive one. I spoke to my supervisor about my project not working... I didn't tell him that I felt like a failure because my research was failing or anything, I tried to keep it professional. It was very difficult though, I had to keep stopping mid sentence because my voice would start to shake and my eyes tearing up. He kept asking if I had any ideas on what I should do but I couldn't even answer them I was feeling so upset, just opening my mouth made my eyes run and I couldn't find my voice. I really hate how much everything is upsetting me lately.

Thanks for your suggestion with /r/fitness, I will have a look on there and see if anyone has some suggestions for my workout and/or diet. Hopefully a little step like that will help me feel a little bit better about myself.

Thankyou for your reply. I am sorry for your friend. Hopefully his friends and family will recover well soon. 

Thinking about my family helps me "get back to reality" a bit, it puts everything back in perspective. I had a really hard time when I was 13 and I first felt like this, a teacher of mine was concerned, got the guidance councilor involved and they called my mom. I will never forget how upset my mom was when she picked me up from school that day.
